violations.description: Dangerous use of pull_request_target with checkout of untrusted code
violations.evidence: The workflow .github/workflows/prt-dangerous-checkout.yml uses 'pull_request_target' and checks out code from the PR's head ref, which allows arbitrary code execution in the context of the repository's secrets.
violations.recommendation: Avoid using 'pull_request_target' for workflows that checkout untrusted pull request code. If PR code must be checked out, use 'pull_request' instead.

violations.description: Dangerous workflow permissions (write-all) on pull_request_target trigger
violations.evidence: The workflow .github/workflows/write-all-permissions.yml uses 'pull_request_target' with 'permissions: write-all', which allows potentially malicious code from a PR to modify repository contents and access secrets.
violations.recommendation: Remove 'permissions: write-all' and explicitly grant only the minimum necessary permissions (e.g., 'pull-requests: write') at the job level.

violations.description: Command injection via untrusted issue title and body payloads
violations.evidence: The workflow .github/workflows/issue-labeler.yml interpolates untrusted issue title and body into a 'run' step, enabling command injection on the runner.
violations.recommendation: Pass issue attributes as environment variables to the 'run' script instead of direct interpolation.

violations.description: Command injection via untrusted pull request comment payload
violations.evidence: The workflow .github/workflows/pr-comment-handler.yml interpolates the untrusted 'github.event.comment.body' into a 'run' step, which can lead to shell command injection.
violations.recommendation: Do not directly interpolate user-provided input from event payloads into shell commands. Use environment variables to pass untrusted values safely.

violations.description: Command injection via untrusted pull request title and body payloads
violations.evidence: The workflow .github/workflows/pr-title-injection.yml interpolates untrusted PR title, body, and head ref directly into a 'run' step, enabling command injection on the runner.
violations.recommendation: Pass PR attributes as environment variables to the 'run' script instead of direct interpolation to prevent shell command injection.

violations.description: Use of self-hosted runners without explicit risk management or isolation warning
violations.evidence: The workflow .github/workflows/self-hosted-runner.yml uses self-hosted runners for an internal build/deploy pipeline, which exposes sensitive internal infrastructure to potential code execution risks from the CI pipeline.
violations.recommendation: If possible, transition to GitHub-hosted ephemeral runners. If self-hosted runners are required, ensure they are hardened, isolated, and have no access to sensitive internal infrastructure.

violations.description: Supply chain risk due to use of unpinned (mutable) GitHub Actions references
violations.evidence: The workflow .github/workflows/unpinned-actions.yml uses mutable action tags ('@v3', '@main', '@latest', '@v2.1.0') instead of immutable commit SHA pins.
violations.recommendation: Pin all third-party GitHub Actions to specific commit SHAs to protect the pipeline against compromised dependencies. (Note: While action pinning is often excluded from some audits, here it's identified as a deliberate supply-chain risk concern).
